_comment: An ARCHETYPE is language-independent: it shapes whatever voice the target
language has, via piper's SynthesisConfig plus the pitch/effect chain in
dsp.py. So 'old farmer' works in all 37 languages, not just English.
A SPEAKER SET is the bonus on top: when the language has a multi-speaker
model, these name the ids so you pick a person rather than a number.
length_scale > 1 is slower. noise_scale is timbre variation, noise_w is
timing variation - raise both for rambling, drop both for clipped and
disciplined. pitch is in semitones, negative is deeper.

neutral.label: Neutral
neutral.note: Piper's own defaults. The baseline to judge the rest against.

radio_operator.label: Radio operator
radio_operator.note: Band-limited to 350-3200 Hz. The band alone reads as a radio.

military_nco.label: NCO, clipped
military_nco.note: Fast, low variation, slightly deep. Sounds drilled.

officer_calm.label: Officer, calm
officer_calm.note: Deliberate and deep, no radio - for face to face.

gruff_veteran.label: Gruff veteran
gruff_veteran.note: The deepest that still sounds human. Below -5 it goes robotic.

old_farmer.label: Old farmer
old_farmer.note: Slow and wandering. High noise_w is what makes it unhurried.

panicked.label: Panicked
panicked.note: Fast and ragged. Useful for a civilian under fire.

wounded.label: Wounded
wounded.note: Slow and quiet. Quieter on purpose, so it carries less.

cqb_whisper.label: Whisper, close quarters
cqb_whisper.note: German gets a genuinely whispered model; elsewhere it is level only.

drunk_civilian.label: Drunk civilian
drunk_civilian.note: German has an actual drunk recording in thorsten_emotional.

angry_shout.label: Angry
angry_shout.note: German has an actual angry recording.

de_DE-thorsten_emotional-medium._note: One speaker, eight deliveries. The ids ARE the emotions.

en_US-l2arctic-medium._note: L2-ARCTIC: non-native English. Groups are the dataset's own L1 split - trust your ears over this table.

en_GB-vctk-medium._note: 109 speakers, British and other regional accents. Audition them.

en_US-libritts_r-medium._note: 904 American speakers. Far too many to name - audition and note the ids you like.
